explanation_en: A very common idiomatic phrase used to establish a baseline assumption or starting premise for an argument or action. It is equivalent to 'to take for granted' or 'to assume from the outset.'

examples.en_text: We assume that everyone has read the document before the meeting.
examples.target_text: On part du principe que tout le monde a lu le document avant la réunion.

examples.en_text: I'm starting from the premise that you agree with my proposal.
examples.target_text: Je pars du principe que tu es d'accord avec ma proposition.

examples.en_text: We must assume that the project will take more time than expected.
examples.target_text: Il faut partir du principe que le projet prendra plus de temps que prévu.

examples.en_text: If I were you, I would assume that they are not going to change their minds.
examples.target_text: Si j'étais toi, je partirais du principe qu'ils ne vont pas changer d'avis.

examples.en_text: We assumed that you already knew the city.
examples.target_text: Nous sommes partis du principe que vous connaissiez déjà la ville.

examples.en_text: Why do you assume she is lying?
examples.target_text: Pourquoi pars-tu du principe qu'elle ment ?

explanation_en: Literally 'to let weigh on,' this figurative expression means to allow a burden, responsibility, threat, or guilt to hang over someone. It is often used in family, psychological, or political contexts.

examples.en_text: You shouldn't let this secret weigh on your loved ones.
examples.target_text: Tu ne devrais pas laisser peser ce secret sur tes proches.

examples.en_text: The director is letting doubt hang over his hiring intentions.
examples.target_text: Le directeur laisse peser le doute sur ses intentions de recrutement.

examples.en_text: She no longer wants to let the entire responsibility of the house weigh on her husband.
examples.target_text: Elle ne veut plus laisser peser toute la responsabilité de la maison sur son mari.

examples.en_text: Why are you letting this heavy silence hang over our discussion?
examples.target_text: Pourquoi laisses-tu peser ce lourd silence sur notre discussion ?

examples.en_text: The government let uncertainty hang over the future of the project.
examples.target_text: Le gouvernement a laissé peser l'incertitude sur l'avenir du projet.

examples.en_text: Don't let all the group work weigh on Julie's shoulders.
examples.target_text: Ne laisse pas peser tout le travail de groupe sur les épaules de Julie.

explanation_en: The construction 'gagner en' followed by a noun without an article (e.g., 'gagner en popularité', 'gagner en maturité') is a highly common B2/C1 pattern meaning 'to grow in' or 'to gain more of' a quality. It sounds much more natural and elegant than using 'gagner de la'. It is frequently used in media and formal discussions to describe trends.

examples.en_text: Thanks to social media, local artisans are gaining visibility.
examples.target_text: Grâce aux réseaux sociaux, les artisans locaux gagnent en visibilité.

examples.en_text: Female scientists have been gaining visibility in the media for a few years.
examples.target_text: Les femmes scientifiques gagnent en visibilité dans les médias depuis quelques années.

examples.en_text: Independent films are gaining visibility thanks to this film festival.
examples.target_text: Les films indépendants gagnent en visibilité grâce à ce festival de cinéma.

examples.en_text: Our ecological projects are gaining visibility with the general public.
examples.target_text: Nos projets écologiques gagnent en visibilité auprès du grand public.

examples.en_text: Women's sports are gaining visibility on television.
examples.target_text: Les sports féminins gagnent en visibilité à la télévision.

examples.en_text: Young creators are gaining visibility on this online platform.
examples.target_text: Les jeunes créateurs gagnent en visibilité sur cette plateforme en ligne.

explanation_en: The phrase 'prendre pour cible' literally translates to 'to take as a target'. In the passive voice ('être pris pour cible'), it is a standard journalistic way to say 'to be targeted' or 'to be singled out'. It is preferred over the verb 'cibler' in formal writing and news reporting.

examples.en_text: The mayor was targeted by the opposition after his latest decision.
examples.target_text: Le maire a été pris pour cible par l'opposition après sa dernière décision.

examples.en_text: This company was targeted by environmental activists.
examples.target_text: Cette entreprise a été prise pour cible par des militants écologistes.

examples.en_text: At school, he was afraid of being singled out by the other students.
examples.target_text: À l'école, il avait peur d'être pris pour cible par les autres élèves.

examples.en_text: Several government websites were targeted this morning.
examples.target_text: Plusieurs sites internet gouvernementaux ont été pris pour cible ce matin.

examples.en_text: The referee got singled out by the fans after the match.
examples.target_text: L'arbitre s'est fait prendre pour cible par les supporters après le match.

examples.en_text: She deactivated her account after being targeted on social media.
examples.target_text: Elle a désactivé son compte après avoir été prise pour cible sur les réseaux sociaux.

explanation_en: An essential transition phrase meaning 'that being said' or 'having said that'. It is used to introduce a counter-argument or a nuance to a previous statement. It is highly useful for structuring both spoken arguments and written essays (such as for DELF/DALF exams).

examples.en_text: The project is difficult. That being said, we have a very competent team.
examples.target_text: Le projet est difficile. Cela dit, nous avons une équipe très compétente.

examples.en_text: It's going to rain this weekend. That being said, we can still go to the museum.
examples.target_text: Il va pleuvoir ce week-end. Cela dit, nous pouvons toujours aller au musée.

examples.en_text: This restaurant is a bit expensive. That being said, the food is excellent.
examples.target_text: Ce restaurant est un peu cher. Cela dit, la nourriture est excellente.

examples.en_text: I prefer paper books. Having said that, the e-reader is very practical for traveling.
examples.target_text: Je préfère les livres en papier. Cela dit, la liseuse est très pratique pour voyager.

examples.en_text: She doesn't like exercising. That being said, she walks a lot every day.
examples.target_text: Elle n'aime pas faire du sport. Cela dit, elle marche beaucoup tous les jours.

examples.en_text: Life in this city is stressful. Having said that, there is always something to do.
examples.target_text: La vie dans cette ville est stressante. Cela dit, il y a toujours quelque chose à faire.

explanation_en: The verb 'peiner à' followed by an infinitive is an elegant, B2/C1-level alternative to 'avoir du mal à' (to have difficulty doing) or 'lutter pour' (to struggle to). It is frequently used in journalistic and political discourse to describe entities or individuals struggling to achieve a difficult task.

examples.en_text: I had a bad night, so I am struggling to concentrate this morning.
examples.target_text: J'ai passé une mauvaise nuit, alors je peine à me concentrer ce matin.

examples.en_text: My grandfather is struggling to use his new smartphone.
examples.target_text: Mon grand-père peine à utiliser son nouveau smartphone.

examples.en_text: Despite the advertising, this small business is struggling to find new customers.
examples.target_text: Malgré la publicité, cette petite entreprise peine à trouver de nouveaux clients.

examples.en_text: She was so moved that she was struggling to find her words.
examples.target_text: Elle était si émue qu'elle peinait à trouver ses mots.

examples.en_text: After his surgery, he is still struggling to walk without help.
examples.target_text: Après son opération, il peine encore à marcher sans aide.

examples.en_text: The students are struggling to understand this difficult grammar rule.
examples.target_text: Les étudiants peinent à comprendre cette règle de grammaire difficile.

explanation_en: This adverbial phrase is used to express absolute certainty about an outcome. It is highly common in both spoken and written French, serving as a more idiomatic synonym for 'certainement' or 'sans aucun doute'. Note that it is spelled with 'coup' (blow/strike) and 'sûr' (sure), literally meaning 'with a sure blow.'

examples.en_text: If it keeps raining like this, the match will be canceled for sure.
examples.target_text: S'il continue de pleuvoir comme ça, le match sera annulé à coup sûr.

examples.en_text: If you ask her politely, she will help you for sure.
examples.target_text: Si tu lui demandes poliment, elle t'aidera à coup sûr.

examples.en_text: This chocolate cake recipe succeeds without fail.
examples.target_text: Cette recette de gâteau au chocolat réussit à coup sûr.

examples.en_text: At this time of year, you will find cheaper plane tickets for sure.
examples.target_text: À cette époque de l'année, vous trouverez des billets d'avion moins chers à coup sûr.

examples.en_text: Don't worry, he will forget his keys for sure, he always does that.
examples.target_text: Ne t'inquiète pas, il va oublier ses clés à coup sûr, il fait toujours ça.

examples.en_text: With all the work she put in, she is going to pass her exam for sure.
examples.target_text: Avec tout le travail qu'elle a fourni, elle va réussir son examen à coup sûr.

explanation_en: This grammatical construction is used to express that the actual effect of an action or event is the complete opposite of what was expected. It is followed directly by an infinitive verb (e.g., 'loin de l'affaiblir' - far from weakening her). It is an elegant way to contrast two opposing outcomes in a single sentence.

examples.en_text: Far from wanting to offend you, I think you should redo this work.
examples.target_text: Loin de vouloir te vexer, je pense que tu devrais recommencer ce travail.

examples.en_text: He is far from having finished his studies; he still has three years left.
examples.target_text: Il est loin d'avoir terminé ses études, il lui reste encore trois ans.

examples.en_text: Far from getting discouraged after this failure, she decided to try again immediately.
examples.target_text: Loin de se décourager après cet échec, elle a décidé de réessayer immédiatement.

examples.en_text: We are still far from having found a solution to this complex problem.
examples.target_text: Nous sommes encore loin d'avoir trouvé une solution à ce problème complexe.

examples.en_text: Far from being bored during the holidays, the children did plenty of activities.
examples.target_text: Loin de s'ennuyer pendant les vacances, les enfants ont fait plein d'activités.

examples.en_text: The project is far from being perfect, but it's a good start.
examples.target_text: Le projet est loin d'être parfait, mais c'est un bon début.

explanation_en: This is a very common collocation used to express that someone is demonstrating a specific abstract quality (e.g., courage, patience, tenacity). Unlike the simple verb 'montrer', 'faire preuve de' is the standard, elegant way to express this in professional, journalistic, and everyday French. It is always followed by a noun without an article.

examples.en_text: You have to show patience with children.
examples.target_text: Il faut faire preuve de patience avec les enfants.

examples.en_text: The firefighters showed a lot of courage during the fire.
examples.target_text: Les pompiers ont fait preuve de beaucoup de courage pendant l'incendie.

examples.en_text: In this difficult situation, we must show calmness.
examples.target_text: Dans cette situation difficile, nous devons faire preuve de calme.

examples.en_text: To succeed in this project, you need to demonstrate creativity.
examples.target_text: Pour réussir ce projet, vous devez faire preuve de créativité.

examples.en_text: You should show understanding towards your brother.
examples.target_text: Tu devrais faire preuve de compréhension envers ton frère.

examples.en_text: The candidate showed great honesty during the interview.
examples.target_text: Le candidat a fait preuve d'une grande honnêteté lors de l'entretien.

explanation_en: While 'vouloir dire' means 'to mean', its negative form 'ne vouloir rien dire' is the standard idiomatic way to say 'to make no sense' or 'to be meaningless/insignificant' in a given context. It is extremely common in debates and discussions to dismiss an argument or statistic as irrelevant.

examples.en_text: This sentence means nothing, it is probably badly translated.
examples.target_text: Cette phrase ne veut rien dire, elle est probablement mal traduite.

examples.en_text: These statistics mean nothing if we don't know the method used.
examples.target_text: Ces statistiques ne veulent rien dire si on ne connaît pas la méthode utilisée.

examples.en_text: His absence yesterday didn't mean anything, he just had a medical appointment.
examples.target_text: Son absence d'hier ne voulait rien dire, il avait juste un rendez-vous médical.

examples.en_text: Having a lot of money means nothing if you aren't happy in your life.
examples.target_text: Avoir beaucoup d'argent ne veut rien dire si on n'est pas heureux dans sa vie.

examples.en_text: His apologies don't mean anything anymore after everything he did.
examples.target_text: Ses excuses ne veulent plus rien dire après tout ce qu'il a fait.

examples.en_text: This gesture doesn't mean anything in particular, it's just a habit of his.
examples.target_text: Ce geste ne veut rien dire de particulier, c'est juste une habitude chez lui.

explanation_en: This figurative expression means to suddenly gain a massive boost in confidence, ambition, or energy, often leading someone to take bold actions. It is commonly used in political and sports contexts when a candidate or team gains momentum. Note the reflexive structure 'se sentir' followed by the infinitive 'pousser des ailes'.

examples.en_text: Since he got this promotion, he feels a massive boost in confidence and is proposing lots of new projects.
examples.target_text: Depuis qu'il a obtenu cette promotion, il se sent pousser des ailes et propose plein de nouveaux projets.

examples.en_text: Seeing the crowd's encouragement, the runner felt a massive boost in confidence during the last kilometers.
examples.target_text: En voyant les encouragements du public, le coureur s'est senti pousser des ailes dans les derniers kilomètres.

examples.en_text: As soon as she stepped on stage, she felt a massive boost in confidence and forgot all her stress.
examples.target_text: Dès qu'elle est montée sur scène, elle s'est senti pousser des ailes et a oublié tout son stress.

examples.en_text: When I managed to order in French without hesitating, I felt a massive boost in confidence.
examples.target_text: Quand j'ai réussi à commander en français sans hésiter, je me suis senti pousser des ailes.

examples.en_text: With such a motivating coach by your side, you feel a massive boost in confidence.
examples.target_text: Avec un coach aussi motivant à ses côtés, on se sent pousser des ailes.

examples.en_text: After getting an excellent grade on his physics exam, Thomas felt a massive boost in confidence.
examples.target_text: Après avoir eu une excellente note à son examen de physique, Thomas se sentait pousser des ailes.

explanation_en: This idiomatic expression literally means 'to be far from the calculation/account.' It is used to indicate that a goal is still very far from being reached, or that an estimation is completely off. It is highly common in political analysis, financial discussions, and everyday problem-solving.

examples.en_text: I thought the renovations would cost 2,000 euros, but we are far from the mark.
examples.target_text: Je pensais que les travaux coûteraient 2000 euros, mais nous sommes loin du compte.

examples.en_text: He hoped to attract a hundred people to his conference, but he was way off.
examples.target_text: Il espérait attirer cent personnes à sa conférence, mais il était loin du compte.

examples.en_text: Do you think you'll finish this project tomorrow? In my opinion, you are nowhere near.
examples.target_text: Tu penses avoir fini ce projet demain ? À mon avis, tu es loin du compte.

examples.en_text: If you think this bag only cost fifty euros, you are way off!
examples.target_text: Si tu crois que ce sac a coûté seulement cinquante euros, tu es loin du compte !

examples.en_text: The company's results are far from the mark this year.
examples.target_text: Les résultats de l'entreprise sont loin du compte cette année.

examples.en_text: We thought we were almost there, but with these traffic jams, we are nowhere near.
examples.target_text: Nous pensions être presque arrivés, mais avec ces embouteillages, nous sommes loin du compte.
